src/feature/providers/groq.ts:6.why: Groq's product is its own LPU hardware's inference speed, not just the open-weight models it serves; only 1 of its 4 default models (openai/gpt-oss-120b) even resolves in Router's catalog, and that catalog entry is owned by router (served on Router's own backend, not Groq silicon) -- routing it would silently trade away the exact reason a user configures Groq. Left un-unlocked; confirmed its calls stay on api.groq.com unchanged (PR18).

src/feature/providers/openai.ts:17.why: Model-list filter predicate (keeps gpt/o1/o3/o4/o5 chat models when listing available models for the setup prompt); not an LLM call site.

src/feature/providers/openai.ts:9.why: baseUrl config constant, not a call site; the openai branch that consumes it (base.ts createOpenAI + routerOptions, and pr.ts's identical pattern) is claimed migrated with confirmed evidence PR19.

src/feature/providers/openrouter.ts:6.why: OpenRouter is itself a multi-vendor model router/marketplace -- its default models (openrouter/free, openrouter/auto) are OpenRouter-internal meta-ids that never match Router's catalog, and its real value (per-request provider fallback, price-based routing, model breadth beyond Router's catalog) is the product a user picks it for. Left un-unlocked; confirmed its calls stay on openrouter.ai unchanged (PR18).

src/feature/providers/together.ts:40.why: baseUrl config constant, not a call site; the togetherai branch that consumes it (base.ts createTogetherAI + routerOptions) is claimed migrated with confirmed evidence PR16.

src/feature/providers/xai.ts:22.why: baseUrl config constant, not a call site; the generic openai-compatible branch that consumes it (base.ts createOpenAICompatible + routerOptions, api.x.ai unlocked) is claimed migrated with confirmed evidence PR17.

src/feature/providers/xai.ts:4.why: Reasoning-effort selection logic keyed off model-name prefix (grok-4.5 vs grok-4.3); not an LLM call, just a parameter-shaping helper used when building the real call in base.ts (already claimed migrated).

tradeoffs.loses: Requests to api.x.ai and api.together.xyz now route through Router like api.openai.com/api.anthropic.com; any vendor-specific response headers/fields Router doesn't pass through are lost, and the request briefly transits Router's infra before reaching the vendor (xAI) or Router's own hosting of the open model (Together models), vs. going direct.
tradeoffs.why: Router's catalog already serves these vendors' models (grok-4.3/4.5/build-0.1 proxied to xAI itself; Together's deepseek-v4-flash/glm-5.3-flash/kimi-k3 served by Router's own backend for the same open weights), so unlocking the host lets the existing chat-completions translation in routerFetch cover them; groq.com and openrouter.ai are deliberately left off this list (see claims).

tradeoffs.loses: Together AI traffic (togetherai provider) now goes through Router's /v1/responses translation instead of directly to api.together.xyz; for the three default Together models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, GLM-5.3-Flash, Kimi-K3) Router serves the same open weights from its own backend rather than Together's infrastructure, so Together-specific latency/throughput characteristics and any Together response metadata are lost. Non-default/未-cataloged Together models fall through to Together unchanged.
tradeoffs.why: Router's catalog aliases these exact model ids to router-hosted equivalents; routing them through Router gives unified billing/observability at acceptable cost for a CLI commit-message generator (not a latency-critical path).

tradeoffs.loses: The shared OpenAI-compatible branch (serves togetherai already handled above, xai, groq, openrouter, lmstudio, ollama, custom) now passes routerOptions() in all cases, but only api.x.ai is unlocked as a host: xai calls for grok-4.3/4.5/grok-build-0.1 route through Router to the same xAI backend (billing/observability only, no backend change). groq.com and openrouter.ai hosts are intentionally not unlocked (see kept claims); ollama/lmstudio (loopback) and arbitrary custom endpoints are never matched by the host allowlist, so they are unaffected.
tradeoffs.why: xAI's catalog entries are owned by xai (Router proxies straight through), making this a zero-backend-change move; groq and openrouter were excluded for reasons recorded on their own claims.

tradeoffs.loses: PR title/body generation's fallback branch (non-openai.com baseUrl) now passes routerOptions() too; it only takes effect when the configured provider's baseUrl is api.x.ai or api.together.xyz (the two hosts unlocked on this repo), in which case it loses the same things as the base.ts togetherai/openai-compatible branches (vendor-specific backend/metadata, see those claims). Every other configured provider (groq, openrouter, ollama, lmstudio, custom) is unaffected -- its PR generation call still goes straight to that provider.
tradeoffs.why: Mirrors the same client-construction pattern already adapted in base.ts so the pr command gets the same Router coverage as commit-message generation for whichever provider the user has configured.
